blocks.text: Romanian filmmaker Cristian Mungiu is a card-carrying member of a very rare club as a two-time Cannes Film Festival Palme d’Or winner . Not only that, but he has won prizes at Cannes just about with every other film he chose to debut there. Those include his latest Fjord , which is not only Romania’s entry into the International Feature Film Oscar race (it qualifies even with the English language mixed with others), pundits have it as a good shot for a Best Picture and Director nomination among other categories.

blocks.text: This would be sweet because despite all the global acclaim Mungiu has yet to break in at the Oscars, most disappointedly after his first Palme d’Or winner, 2007’s 4 Months, 3 Weeks, And 2 Days , failed to make the cut — a shocker considering the critical support behind it. Other films like Beyond the Hills (2012) and Graduation (2016) and R.M.N. (2022) have kept him at the top of his game, returning him to Cannes every four years. But now it is Fjord , starring Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve as a couple moving to Norway with five children and finding them at odds with local authorities over their parenting and religious beliefs, that is taking the filmmaker to a new level.

Mungiu joins me this week for a new episode of my Deadline video series Behind the Lens where we talk about all of it, plus his hopes for Fjord, the seventh Palme d’Or winner in a row for its distributor Neon, at the Oscars. Just this past weekend it received five nominations at the European Film Awards and seems well on its way to the Dolby Theater in March.
